note_claims.claim: The patient presented with central chest pain starting at about 11:00 while gardening.
The patient experienced heavy central chest pain radiating to the left arm, lasting about 30 minutes, and is currently experiencing pain at a severity of 3/10.
The patient associated the chest pain with sweating and mild breathlessness, but no nausea.
The patient has no previous similar episodes or known cardiac disease.
The patient has a history of hypertension.
The patient is a smoker, smoking about 20 cigarettes per day.
The patient's father had a myocardial infarction at age 52.
The patient's father had a myocardial infarction at age 60.
The patient received aspirin 300 mg and GTN spray from the paramedics.
The patient is taking amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient's heart rate is 88 and regular.
The patient's blood pressure is 152/90.
The patient's oxygen level is 97 percent on air.
The patient's heart sounds are normal.
The patient's chest is clear.
The patient has no swelling in their ankles.
The patient's ECG shows ST depression in the leads on the left side of the chest, V4 to V6, about one millimetre.
The impression is suspected acute coronary syndrome (possible NSTEMI).
The plan includes serial high-sensitivity troponin testing.
The plan is to start fondaparinux 2.5 milligrams subcutaneously once daily to thin the blood.
The plan includes using a GTN spray if the pain returns.
The patient will be admitted under the cardiology team, with a likely plan for coronary angiography.
The patient was instructed to report recurrent or worsening pain to nursing staff immediately.

transcript_facts.fact: Patient reported getting pain in the chest while digging in the garden.
The patient reported the pain started after lunch, but corrected it to 'before' and 'about eleven o'clock' (before eating).
The relative stated the pain started just before eleven, after putting the kettle on.
The patient described the pain as being in the middle of the chest, like a heavy weight.
The patient reported the pain went down their left arm.
The pain lasted about half an hour and is currently at a severity of three out of ten.
The patient reported feeling very sweaty but not sick.
The patient reported feeling a bit short of breath.
The patient stated they have never had this before.
The patient stated they have no heart problems in the past but is on amlodipine.
The patient's amlodipine dose is five milligrams.
The patient stated they have no other medicines.
The patient stated they have no known drug allergies.
The patient stated they smoke about twenty cigarettes a day.
The patient's father had a heart attack at age 52.
The relative stated their father had a heart attack at age 60.
The paramedics gave the patient aspirin 300 milligrams and a GTN spray.
The clinician noted the patient's heart rate is 88 and regular.
The clinician noted the patient's blood pressure is 152 over 90.
The clinician noted the patient's heart sounds are normal.
The clinician noted the patient's chest is clear.
The clinician noted the patient's oxygen level is 97 percent.
The clinician noted the ECG shows about a millimetre of ST depression in the leads on the left side of the chest, V4 to V6.
The clinician interpreted the ST depression as a sign the heart muscle isn't getting enough blood.
The clinician stated it is possible the condition is an acute coronary syndrome.
The clinician stated they have taken a blood test for troponin to check for heart muscle damage.
The clinician stated they will start an injection called fondaparinux, 2.5 milligrams under the skin once a day, to thin the blood.
The clinician stated the patient can have a GTN spray if the pain comes back.
The clinician stated they will admit the patient under the cardiology team, who will likely want to do an angiogram.
The clinician stated they will repeat the ECG every time the patient gets pain.
The clinician instructed the patient to tell the nurses straight away if the pain comes back or gets worse.

findings.note_span: ECG: sinus rhythm, no ST segment changes.
findings.transcript_evidence: Your ECG, the heart tracing, shows some changes. There's about a millimetre of ST depression in the leads on the left side of the chest, V4 to V6.
findings.rationale: The note contradicts the transcript by stating 'no ST segment changes' when the transcript explicitly documents a critical finding of ST depression, which is a major diagnostic error.

findings.transcript_evidence: I'm going to start an injection called fondaparinux, 2.5 milligrams under the skin once a day, to thin the blood.
findings.rationale: The note records an incorrect dose (25 mg) for fondaparinux, which is a significant error in prescribing an anticoagulant.
